# Projects

The sidebar: every folder you work in, with every session in it, from both agents.

![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

The folder, a session and New Session answer the pointer.

## Projects

A project is a folder you have run an agent in. The sidebar lists them all, the newest first, pinned ones on top. Click a project to unfold its sessions. The plus on its row starts a new session there (⌘T in the project you are in, ⌘N anywhere). A project with a live session wears the accent and opens by itself.

Right-click a project to archive or delete its sessions, open it in Finder, or hide it. Hidden projects and the system’s temporary folders sit under their own headings at the foot. Nothing in a project’s own folder is ever touched.

## Sessions

Each session is a row under its project: the agent’s mark, lit while it runs, a dot for where it stands, the title, and a bar at the left when it has a tab. Claude Code and Codex sessions sit side by side, each read from its own files.

**All Sessions** (⌘L) lists every project and every session with the day it was last touched, archived ones under their own heading, and narrows to one agent. Select many at once (⌘-click, ⇧-click, or drag a rectangle), then archive or delete them together.

## Kept and archived

Claude Code deletes its transcripts after thirty days. Emaki copies every one into `~/.emaki/archive` the first time it sees it, so a session the agent has deleted is still listed, searchable and readable, marked *kept*. Codex deletes nothing by age, so its sessions are read in place.

*Archive* a session and the agent leaves it alone until you unarchive it. *Delete* moves every copy to the Trash. Renaming a session renames it for the agent too.

## Search

⌘K searches every session on the machine. One hit per prompt, paragraph, thought or tool call, so a hit lands on the thing you remembered, in live and kept sessions alike.

## Tabs

Every open session is a tab, grouped by project. ⌘1 to ⌘9 switch, ⌘W closes, ⌘⇧T brings back the last one closed, and a drag reorders them.
